confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on 2026 crowd-sourced cost-of-living aggregates found by web search: Numbeo data via Expatica (June 2026), CityCost (July 2026) and Expatistan (July 2026). They were converted from yen at about 159 JPY per USD. Those sources reported an inexpensive meal at JPY 1,202-1,314, a three-course meal for two at JPY 7,010-7,923, a cappuccino at JPY 534-603 and a 0.5 L draught beer at JPY 550-704. The anchors are blends of those figures. Cocktail confidence is lower. One travel guide gave a range of JPY 1,000-2,000, and an Expatistan figure of about JPY 2,082 is based on only 8 data points. A standard bar or restaurant cocktail was estimated at about JPY 1,300-1,400, excluding cover charges. The wine-by-the-glass estimate is weakest. The searches found no reliable Tokyo-wide average, only scattered menu examples and hotel prices of about JPY 1,900-2,000. The estimate of about JPY 850-900 for a typical restaurant glass is based on its relationship to the beer price and on general knowledge. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, with no searches or listing checks. They assume July 2026 peak-summer demand, strong inbound tourism and recent price inflation for Tokyo hotels. Actual rates may vary by about ±25% depending on district and dates.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable-city substitution was needed for food and drink, because Tokyo-specific aggregated price data was available. Accommodation estimates are based on general knowledge of Tokyo's market. Hostel dorms and private rooms are typically priced well above Southeast Asian levels. Basic business hotels are often similar in price to private hostel rooms, and standard three-star hotels cost much more in peak season. These levels are broadly comparable to Seoul at the low end and to major Western European capitals for three-star hotels.
